page: Amazon Web Services c6g.medium is an entry-level compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by custom AWS Graviton processors built on the 64-bit ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture. The instance is allocated 1 dedicated physical core and 1 vCPU operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. Its CPU cache structure consists of 64 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache, with hardware acceleration support for AES cryptographic operations.

The configuration provides 2.0 GB of memory, maintaining the typical 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of the compute-optimized family. It includes no bundled local storage, relying on network-attached storage options, and features zero GPUs. Network throughput is listed at a 0 Gbps baseline, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Performance benchmarks reflect the constrained single-core capacity of an entry tier. The stress-ng single-core test reaches 1493.38, placing it in the average range, whereas multi-core throughput mirrors this score due to the single-vCPU limitation. Across broader testing, including Geekbench (single-core score of 934.0, multi-core score of 933.0) and PassMark CPU (660.71), results fall into the lower tiers compared to larger multi-threaded instances. Memory bandwidth measures 59.29 GB/s for cached 16 KB read blocks, dropping to 19.65 GB/s on uncached 256 MB reads and 9.83 GB/s on writes.

In operational benchmarks, the instance delivers 1.19 million Redis SET operations per second and 1.11 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Inferencing with a small 135M language model achieves 38.25 tokens per second for prompt processing and 29.22 tokens per second for text generation. The c6g.medium serves as a cost-efficient ARM64 testbed, suited for lightweight microservices, dev/test environments, low-traffic web serving, and basic background worker processes.
